cohort: 1748 pregnant women who had spontaneous vaginal births between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2017, in a single birth centre in Portugal
finding: The prevalence of intact perineum was 25.2%, and predictive factors included birth weight, parity, previous caesarean section, and birthing position.
mod_finding: Alternative birth positions (excluding lithotomy) were associated with  double the odds of maintaining an intact perineum.
